CHLORALUM.

Hydrate  of  Chloral  C^HGl^  0+H^  0.


Discovered  in  1832,  by  Lieblg.

Proved  by  W.  Eggert,  S.  Swan,  D.  A.  Babcock,  etc.     See  Encyclopedia,  v.  3.

Poisoning,  by  E.  W.  Berridge,  N.  Y.  J.  H.,  v.  2,  p.  307.

"  Prepared  by  passing  a  stream  of  chlorine  through  absolute  alcohol,  until  it
comes  over  unchanged.  The  thick  fluid  remaining  behind  is  chloral.  The  simple
addition  of  water  converts  chloral  into  its  hydrate."

The  first  therapeutic  application  of  this  substance  was  made  by  O.  Liebreich,
of  Berlin,  who  conceived  that  the  transformation  of  chloral  into  chloroform  might
be  expected  when  it  reached  the  blood  of  a  living  animal.  On  coming  into  contact
with  its  alkalis  the  chloral  would  separate  into  chloroform  and  formicic  acid.

W.  W.  Keen,  of  Philadelphia,  has  made  use  of  chloral  as  an  antiseptic  and
deodorant  in  the  dissecting  room  and  in  surgical  practice.
